security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel (KVM, context-switch, or interrupt handling) accesses Smnmi/Smcip CSRs using the pre-correction CSR addresses (e.g., mithreshold at 0xFB1, sithreshold at 0x1B1, msp at 0x348, ssp at 0x148) instead of the corrected final addresses, causing reads/writes to alias into wrong CSRs on hardware that implements the final spec.
security_spec.summary: Incorrect CSR addresses in kernel headers would alias Smnmi interrupt-control CSRs (mithreshold→0xFB1 was mipreemptcfg, msp→0x348 is now mipreemptcfg, ssp→0x148 was sithreshold) onto different registers, enabling guest-to-host CSR write escalation in KVM and corrupting interrupt preemption/delivery state across context switches

findings.finding: No Smnmi/Smcip CSR address constants (pre-correction or otherwise) are defined in this file. The vulnerability pattern targets CSR addresses 0xFB1 (mithreshold), 0x1B1 (sithreshold), 0x348 (msp/mipreemptcfg), 0x148 (ssp), 0x346 (mpistatus), 0x146 (spistatus) — none of these appear anywhere in lines 251-610. The only CSR_SSP defined (line 336) is 0x011 for Zicfiss shadow stack, which is unrelated to the Smcip supervisor SSP. The kernel has no Smnmi/Smcip support at all at this revision, so there is nothing to mis-address.
findings.snippet:
/* zicfiss user mode csr.  CSR_SSP holds current shadow stack pointer */
#define CSR_SSP            0x011

#define CSR_MEPC            0x341
#define CSR_MCAUSE          0x342
#define CSR_MTVAL           0x343
